chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' said:

We mentioned the *luqatah* (found property) to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Do not expose it (for people to see), for if people were to leave it, its owner would come until he takes it.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.اَللُّقَطَة: Found property or lost item picked up from the ground
key_terms.لاَ تَعَرَّضْ: Do not expose or make it accessible/visible

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended action when finding lost property according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a practical legal principle regarding *luqatah* (found property), advising against public announcement to prevent unnecessary disruption. The reasoning reflects a presumption of the owner's proximity or likelihood of return, contrasting with other juristic opinions that mandate broader publicity. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing property rights with social convenience and minimizing public disturbance.
